ja: うちの課長は、電車の遅れは私たちにはどうしようもなかったのに、お客様を待たせたことを心から謝っていた。
en: My manager apologized sincerely to the client for keeping them waiting, even though the train delay was out of our control.
alternatives: Even though the train delay was beyond our control, my manager sincerely apologized to the client for keeping them waiting.
My manager sincerely apologized to the client for keeping them waiting, even though we couldn't do anything about the train delay.
point: 「〜のに」は even though、待たせる は keep 人 waiting

ja: 私のミスのせいで、チーム全員に週末出勤させることになってしまって、本当に申し訳ない。
en: I'm truly sorry that my mistake made the whole team come in on the weekend.
alternatives: I'm really sorry my mistake forced the whole team to work over the weekend.
I'm so sorry. Because of my mistake, the whole team had to come in on the weekend.
point: make + 人 + 動詞の原形。to は付けない

ja: 君の助けがなかったら、今もまだこの報告書で行き詰まっていたところだよ。手伝ってくれて本当にありがとう。
en: If it weren't for your help, I'd still be stuck on this report. Thanks so much for pitching in.
alternatives: Without your help, I'd still be stuck on this report. Thank you so much for pitching in.
If you hadn't helped me, I'd still be stuck on this report, so thanks a lot for helping out.
point: 今も続く状況の仮定は I'd still be で表す

ja: 引っ越しを手伝ってくれてありがとう。本当に困っていたんだ。
en: Thanks for helping me move. I was really struggling.
alternatives: Thank you for helping me move. I was really having a hard time.
Thanks for your help with the move. I was really struggling.
point: 「困っていた」は過去進行形 was struggling で表せる

ja: ミスしてすみません。次はダブルチェックします。
en: Sorry for the mistake. I'll double-check next time.
alternatives: I'm sorry about the mistake. I will double-check next time.
Sorry about the mistake. I'll double-check it next time.
point: その場で決めた約束は will。the mistake の冠詞も忘れずに

ja: ミスをしたのは私なので、私から部長に謝るべきです。
en: I made the mistake, so I should apologize to the manager.
alternatives: It was my mistake, so I should apologize to the manager.
I'm the one who made the mistake, so I should apologize to the manager.
point: apologize は自動詞なので to を忘れない

ja: 今回ご迷惑をおかけしたのは、チームのミスではなく、私が数字の確認を怠ったせいです。申し訳ありません。
en: It was my failure to check the figures, not a mistake by the team, that caused this inconvenience. I sincerely apologize.
alternatives: What caused this inconvenience was my failure to check the figures, not a mistake by the team. I sincerely apologize.
It was my failure to check the numbers, not the team's mistake, that caused this trouble. I sincerely apologize.
point: It was A, not B, that で「B ではなく A が」を強調

ja: 彼女の誕生日パーティーに行けなかったこと、ちゃんと謝っておけばよかったな。
en: I wish I'd apologized properly to her for missing her birthday party.
alternatives: I wish I had properly apologized to her for not going to her birthday party.
If only I'd apologized to her properly for missing her birthday party.
point: 過去への後悔は wish の後を過去完了にする

ja: 新人の田中くんがミスに気づいてなかったら、私たち、お客さんに間違った見積もりを送ってたよ。ちゃんとお礼言わなきゃ。
en: If our new hire Tanaka hadn't spotted the mistake, we'd have sent the client the wrong quote. We should thank him properly.
alternatives: If Tanaka, our new hire, hadn't caught the mistake, we'd have sent the client the wrong quote. We should really thank him.
We'd have sent the client the wrong quote if our new guy Tanaka hadn't noticed the mistake. We need to thank him properly.
point: 過去の事実の裏は If S had done, S would have done

ja: 越してきたばかりで心細かったので、近所を案内してもらえたことが何より嬉しかったです。ありがとうございました。
en: What I appreciated most was that you showed me around the neighborhood when I'd just moved in and felt a bit lost. Thank you.
alternatives: What meant the most to me was that you showed me around the neighborhood when I'd just moved in and felt a little lost. Thank you.
The thing I appreciated most was you showing me around the neighborhood when I'd just moved here and was feeling uneasy. Thank you.
point: 「何より嬉しかったこと」を主語にして was で受ける

ja: 先輩が夜中まで残ってスライドの修正を手伝ってくれたから、お礼にランチをおごったんだ。
en: My senior coworker stayed until midnight helping me fix the slides, so I bought them lunch as a thank-you.
alternatives: My senior colleague stayed till midnight helping me fix the slides, so I treated them to lunch.
My senior coworker stayed until midnight helping me with the slides, so I bought them lunch to say thanks.
point: 「残って手伝う」は stayed helping と -ing でつなぐ

ja: さっき君が車で送ってくれなかったら、僕は今ごろまだ駅で待ってたよ。ほんとにありがとう！
en: If you hadn't driven me here, I'd still be waiting at the station right now. Thanks so much!
alternatives: If you hadn't given me a ride, I'd still be waiting at the station right now. Thank you so much!
Thanks so much! If you hadn't driven me, I'd still be stuck waiting at the station now.
point: 過去の条件＋今の結果は If I had done, I'd be doing

ja: 送る前にちゃんと確認するべきでした。ミスしてしまって申し訳ありません。
en: I should have checked it before sending it. I'm sorry about the mistake.
alternatives: I should've double-checked it before I sent it. I'm sorry for the mistake.
I should have checked it before sending. I apologize for the error.
point: 「〜すべきだった」は should have + 過去分詞

ja: あの朝あなたが車で送ってくれなかったら、私は面接に間に合わなかったと思います。本当にありがとうございました。
en: If you hadn't given me a ride that morning, I don't think I'd have made it to the interview. Thank you so much.
alternatives: I don't think I would have made it to the interview if you hadn't driven me that morning. Thank you so much.
If you hadn't driven me that morning, I probably wouldn't have gotten to the interview in time. I really appreciate it.
point: 過去の仮定は had 過去分詞、帰結は would have 過去分詞

ja: 昨日は電話に出られなくてごめんね。電車に乗ってたんだ。
en: Sorry I couldn't answer your call yesterday. I was on the train.
alternatives: Sorry I couldn't pick up your call yesterday. I was on the train.
Sorry I couldn't take your call yesterday. I was on a train.
point: 過去の「できなかった」は couldn't で表す

ja: こんなに迷惑をかけてしまったので、今週末に埋め合わせをさせてもらえませんか？
en: Could you let me make it up to you this weekend for all the trouble I've caused?
alternatives: Would you let me make it up to you this weekend for all the trouble I caused?
Can I make it up to you this weekend for causing you so much trouble?
point: 埋め合わせる は make it up to 人

ja: 先日お貸しいただいた資料を、まだお返ししていなくて申し訳ありません。
en: I'm sorry I still haven't returned the documents that you lent me the other day.
alternatives: I'm sorry I haven't returned the materials you lent me the other day yet.
I apologize that I still haven't returned the documents you lent me the other day.
point: 「まだ〜していない」は still haven't returned

ja: 遅れてすみません。もう一度最初から説明していただけますか？
en: Sorry I'm late. Could you explain it again from the beginning?
alternatives: I'm sorry I'm late. Could you go over it again from the start?
Sorry for being late. Would you explain it again from the beginning?
point: 丁寧な依頼は Could you + 動詞の原形

ja: お客さんに送る前にミスに気づいてくれて、ありがとう。
en: Thanks for catching the mistake before we sent it to the client.
alternatives: Thank you for noticing the mistake before we sent it to the client.
Thanks for spotting the mistake before we sent it to the client.
point: before の後は過去形 sent で時制をそろえる

ja: 手伝ってくれてありがとう。君は本当に優しいね。
en: Thanks for your help. You're so kind.
alternatives: Thank you for helping me. You're really kind.
Thanks for the help. You're very kind.
point: 「優しい」は be 動詞＋kind。You kind としない
